### Estimated Time of Departure (Logistics & Travel)

- **Definition:** The planned date and time when a vehicle, ship, aircraft, or cargo shipment is expected to leave its origin or port.
- **Usage:** Used alongside **ETA** (Estimated Time of Arrival) to track schedules and plan supply chains.
- **Context:** If a cargo ship has an ETD of 08:00 tomorrow, it is expected to pull away from the dock at that time, though weather or traffic can cause it to change.[[1]](https://outvio.com/blog/eta-etd/)[[2]](https://www.stonex.com/en-us/business/financial-glossary/etd-shipping/)[[3]](https://www.stonex.com/en/business/financial-glossary/etd-shipping/)[[4]](https://ntslogistics.com/glossary/meaning-of-estimated-time-of-departure/)[[5]](https://www.dhl.com/discover/en-hk/logistics-advice/essential-guides/mastering-logistics-terminology)

### Eustachian Tube Dysfunction (Medicine)

- **Definition:** A common ear condition where the tubes connecting your middle ear to your upper throat fail to open or close properly.
- **Symptoms:** Muffled hearing, ear popping, a feeling of fullness or pressure in the ear, and mild balance issues.
- **Causes:** Allergies, sinus infections, colds, or sudden changes in altitude.[[1]](https://rkaudiology.com/etd-meaning-what-eustachian-tube-dysfunction-means-for-your-ears/)[[2]](https://my.clevelandclinic.org/health/diseases/22527-eustachian-tube-dysfunction)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/shorts/tVD6zS3IGjI)
